name: Board notes (knowledge packs for the shipped boards)
author: Biga73 (idea) · DEADBOARD
description: An example data mod: a knowledge pack for every board that ships with DEADBOARD. Rails, where each one comes from, what to expect at which pin, and what a low reading usually means, each marked documented, derived or estimated. The packs describe the working board and point at likely causes, the way the board's hints do; they don't name the planted faults. Based on the device knowledge pack RFC by Biga73.

knowledge.title: First Light

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.expect: ≈3.0 V idle, ≈2.93 V with SW1 pressed
checks.readsLowIf: the cell is flat or its holder doesn't make contact

rails.notes: The cell sags about 70 mV under the LED's 9 mA: that's its internal resistance.

checks.readsLowIf: SW1 doesn't close, or a joint on SW1 is open
R1 is open (then R1 pin 2 reads 0 V while pin 1 reads 2.9 V)
the copper from R1 to D1 is open: compare with R1 pin 2

rails.notes: I = (2.93 − 2.00) V / 100 Ω ≈ 9 mA. If D1 pin 2 reads the full 2.9 V and D1 stays dark, no current flows through D1: it's open or reversed.

notes: Current path: BT1 + → SW1 → R1 → D1 (anode pin 2, cathode pin 1) → BT1 −.

knowledge.title: Cold Joint 101

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the cell is flat
nothing reaches D1 through R1: an open joint or trace on either side of R1 (0 V, and the supply delivers no current)

notes: A through-hole part is soldered on the bottom side: a joint can look fine from the top and still be open.

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the cell is flat, or something downstream draws far more than 9 mA
≈0 V while the supply still delivers current: D1's two pins are shorted together, so the current goes around it

rails.notes: I = (2.93 − 2.00) V / 100 Ω ≈ 9 mA. With D1 shorted, R1 alone limits the current: about 3 V / 100 Ω.

knowledge.title: One-Way LED

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the cell is flat
R1's path is open (0 V). The full cell voltage here with D1 dark means D1 doesn't conduct: open, or fitted the wrong way round

notes: An LED conducts from anode (pin 2) to cathode (pin 1, the flat side of the body and the K mark on the silkscreen).

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the supply isn't connected
too little current reaches D1: R1's value is far above 150 Ω, or a joint on R1 is open. Measure R1 with the power off

rails.notes: I = (5.0 − 3.24) V / 150 Ω ≈ 12 mA (the simulator gives 11.7 mA).

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the supply isn't connected
the bottom resistor R2 is lower than R1, or R1 is open (then ≈0 V)

rails.notes: Vout = 5 V × R2 / (R1 + R2) = 2.50 V with R1 = R2 = 10 kΩ, 0.25 mA through both. Nothing pulling VOUT down (R2 missing or open) leaves it at the full 5 V.

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator (SPICE, 2N3904 model) on the working board

checks.expect: ≈2.8–3.0 V (2.81 V with SW1 pressed: the cells sag under the ≈23 mA load)
checks.readsLowIf: the battery is flat or not connected

checks.expect: ≈0.67 V pressed (one base–emitter diode drop, ≈2.1 mA into the base)
checks.readsLowIf: ≈0 V: SW1 or R1 is open. Close to +3V instead: the base–emitter junction is open (Q1 missing, or its base or emitter lead not soldered)

rails.notes: Released, nothing drives the base: it reads a few hundred mV at most.

rails.domain: both LED cathodes, switched to GND by Q1

checks.readsLowIf: it reads high instead: ≈2 V means Q1 never switches on (no base current, or Q1 open); ≈1.1 V with the LEDs only glowing means Q1 conducts with a gain near 1, i.e. it is fitted backwards

rails.notes: Pressed, each LED takes ≈10.6 mA through its 68 Ω resistor: together ten times the base current (R1 is sized for that, the usual rule for a transistor switch). Released, the collector floats up to ≈2 V. Q1's pins: 1 emitter, 2 base, 3 collector; its flat face matches the D printed on the board.

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.expect: ≈3.0 V idle, ≈2.88 V with SW1 pressed (≈15 mA)
checks.readsLowIf: the cell is flat, or something on BUS draws far more than 15 mA
SW1 doesn't close
no current reaches D1 through R1: an open joint on R1 or D1
≈0 V: D2's pins are shorted together, or R2's path is open

rails.notes: Each LED has its own 100 Ω resistor from BUS: R1 feeds D1, R2 feeds D2. The two branches don't depend on each other, so each can have its own fault.

knowledge.title: Backwards Day

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.expect: ≈5.0 V (≈20 mA with both LEDs lit)
checks.readsLowIf: the supply isn't connected
R1 is a much higher value than 330 Ω, or its path is open
≈0 V at D2 while R2 pin 2 reads 5 V: the copper from R2 to D2 is open

notes: Both LEDs hang straight off +5V, each through its own resistor: R1 330 Ω for the yellow D1, R2 150 Ω for the blue D2.
The full 5 V at an LED's anode with the LED dark means no current flows through it: open, or fitted the wrong way round.

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the supply isn't connected, or it is current-limiting into a short
F1 is open. Before fitting a new one, measure +5V to GND with the power off: a fuse blows for a reason

checks.expect: ≈2.24 V (green LED, ≈5.9 mA through R3 470 Ω)
checks.readsLowIf: +5V is missing, or R3's path is open

rails.notes: Healthy board: ≈6.1 mA from J1 (the LED's 5.9 mA plus 0.25 mA through the divider). A short that blew F1 is on the fuse's output side: one before the fuse would never have blown it.

checks.readsLowIf: +5V is missing, the bottom resistor R2 is lower than R1, or R1 is open

rails.notes: Vout = 5 V × R2 / (R1 + R2) = 2.50 V with R1 = R2 = 10 kΩ.

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the supply isn't connected, or it is current-limiting into a short
F1 is open. Measure VRAIL to GND with the power off before fitting a new one
≈0 V: F1 is open or D1 blocks (fitted the wrong way round). Low but not zero: something leaks from VRAIL to GND

checks.expect: ≈2.30 V (green LED, ≈9 mA through R1 220 Ω)
checks.readsLowIf: VRAIL is low, or R1's path is open

rails.notes: D1 drops ≈0.72 V at 9 mA, so VRAIL sits a diode drop below the input. With the power off, diode mode across D1 reads about 0.7 V with red on the anode (pin 2) and OL the other way round.

knowledge.title: The Sagging Rail

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.readsLowIf: the supply isn't connected
the bottom resistor R2 is a lower value than R1 (10 kΩ), or VREF leaks to GND

rails.notes: Vref = 5 V × R2 / (R1 + R2) = 2.50 V with R1 = R2 = 10 kΩ.

checks.readsLowIf: R3's path is open. The full 5 V here with D1 dark means no current flows through D1: check its path back to GND

notes: This board uses both copper layers: D1's ground return runs through a via and the bottom side to TP2.

knowledge.title: MNT Reform 2 motherboard rev 3.0

provenance.where: set points from source.mnt.re/reform/reform @ c3b7fad and the regulators' datasheets (docs/calibration)

rails.notes: In this demo the bench supply is clipped onto the gated input rail, after the input switch Q15. U7, U9 and U14 all run from it.

provenance.where: the board's description in DEADBOARD

checks.readsLowIf: U14 has no input (30V_GATE at pin 5) or isn't switching, or a part on LPC_VCC pulls it down

rails.notes: U14's EN (pin 4) isn't connected, so LPC_VCC is there as soon as 30V_GATE is. It powers U18, the LPC11U24 system controller, which switches the other rails on.

provenance.where: U14 is the fixed 3.3 V option (Q3 suffix); its FB pin (3) senses the output directly

checks.readsLowIf: 5V_PWR_EN (U7 pin 13) is low, U7 has no input, or a part on +5V pulls the rail down

checks.expect: high (≈3.3 V) once the LPC turns +5V on

rails.notes: Set point: 1.0 V × (1 + R90 100 kΩ / R93 24.9 kΩ) = 5.016 V. 5V_PWR_EN comes from U18 pin 43; R92 holds it low when the LPC doesn't drive it.

provenance.where: LM62460 VFB 1.0 V ±1 % (TI SNVSBZ4A); R90 / R93 as fitted

checks.readsLowIf: 3V3_PWR_EN (U9 pin 13) is low, U9 has no input, or a part on +3V3 pulls the rail down. Enable high and the rail far below target: look for the part that gets hot

checks.expect: high (≈3.3 V) once the LPC turns +3V3 on

rails.notes: Set point: 1.0 V × (1 + R100 100 kΩ / R106 43.2 kΩ) = 3.315 V. 3V3_PWR_EN comes from U18 pin 48; R105 holds it low when the LPC doesn't drive it.

provenance.where: LM62460 VFB 1.0 V ±1 % (TI SNVSBZ4A); R100 / R106 as fitted

checks.readsLowIf: +5V is missing (U13's input, pin 4), or its enable (U13 pin 1) is low

rails.notes: Set point: 0.6 V × (1 + R178 100 kΩ / R179 100 kΩ) = 1.2 V. Enable: U18 pin 2 (1V2_PWR_EN) → R185 (0 Ω) → U13 pin 1; R188 holds it low.

provenance.where: TLV62568 VFB 0.6 V ±2 % (TI SLVSD89B); R178 / R179 as fitted

checks.readsLowIf: +5V is missing (U19's input, pin 4), or its enable (U19 pin 1) is low

rails.notes: Set point: 0.6 V × (1 + R180 150 kΩ / R181 100 kΩ) = 1.5 V. Enable: U18 pin 9 (PCIE1_PWR_EN) → R186 (0 Ω) → U19 pin 1; R189 holds it low.

provenance.where: TLV62568 VFB 0.6 V ±2 % (TI SLVSD89B); R180 / R181 as fitted

notes: Power-up order, worked out from the board (derived): 30V_GATE → U14 (always on) → LPC_VCC → U18 drives the enables → +5V and +3V3 → +1V2 and +1V5, which take +5V as their input. Which rail the LPC switches first within a step is up to its firmware and isn't documented here.
A rail far below its target while its regulator has input and enable is usually being pulled down by a load, not a dead regulator.

knowledge.title: Antmicro Jetson Nano / Xavier NX baseboard

provenance.where: set points from github.com/antmicro/jetson-nano-baseboard @ d8d0b2d and the regulators' datasheets (docs/calibration)

source.kind: input fuse from the bench supply (12 V at the input connector)

rails.notes: The board's README recommends a 12 V 2 A supply (6–36 V input range). In this demo the bench supply is clipped at the input connector, before the input fuse F3: an open F3 shows as a dead VIN. D14 sits across VIN and GND.

checks.readsLowIf: U6 has no input (pin 1), or its enable (pin 3, TP15) is low
the input path from VIN through FB1 is open

rails.notes: Set point: 0.8 V × (1 + R117 52.3 kΩ / R120 10 kΩ) = 4.984 V. R91 (100 kΩ) pulls the enable up from U6's input; TP15 is on the enable.

provenance.where: SiC477 VFB 0.800 V ±1 % over temperature (Vishay doc. 77113); R117 / R120 as fitted

checks.readsLowIf: 5V0_SYS is low, or FB2 or one of its joints is open

provenance.where: FB2 joins 5V0_SYS to the module connector J15

checks.readsLowIf: U2 has no input (pins 8 and 12), its enable (pin 7) is low, or it isn't switching: look at /Supply/3V3_SW with the scope

rails.notes: Fixed 3.3 V option: FB (pin 4) is tied to the output through R48 (0 Ω); 3.2587–3.3413 V. The enable comes through R44 (10 kΩ) from #RESET, the module's reset line on J15 pin 239; RST1 can pull it to GND.

provenance.where: LM62440 fixed 3.3 V trim (TI SNVSAW8E); R48 fitted, R118 / R119 not fitted

notes: Power-up order, worked out from the board (derived): VIN → U6 → 5V0_SYS → FB2 → VDD_MOD (the module). U2 also runs from VIN but is enabled from #RESET, so 3V3_SYS follows the module coming out of reset.
A converter with input and enable present and no output is a dead part; a converter whose input comes and goes when the board is pressed has a cracked joint on its input path.

knowledge.title: OLIMEX ESP32-DevKit-LiPo (Rev. D)

provenance.where: set points from github.com/OLIMEX/ESP32-DevKit-LiPo @ 1ebbbb5 and the parts' datasheets (docs/calibration)

source.kind: bench supply, 5 V on the USB rail

rails.notes: The micro-USB connector USB-UART1 feeds this rail; it also powers the CH340X USB-serial chip U2 (pin 7).

checks.readsLowIf: nothing comes through D1 from the USB rail: the diode or one of its joints is open

rails.notes: One Schottky drop below USB (about 0.3 V with the module running at 80 mA). +5V feeds the charger U1 and, through D2, the regulator. The diode keeps a battery from back-feeding the USB port.

provenance.where: 1N5819 forward curve (Diodes DS30217); the drop depends on the load

source.kind: Schottky diode from +5V; FET1 from VBAT

checks.readsLowIf: D2 is open, or +5V is low

rails.notes: An unnamed net: the regulator's input. On USB it comes through D2; without USB, the P-MOSFET FET1 (gate on +5V) turns on and feeds it from the battery. FET1's body diode conducts the other way only, VBAT towards here.

provenance.where: D2, FET1 (WPM2015, gate on +5V) and U3 pins 1 / 3 share this net

checks.readsLowIf: U3 has no input (pins 1 and 3), the rail is shorted, or U3 is dead

checks.expect: 4.2–4.6 V (input; CE, pin 3, is tied to it)

rails.notes: Fixed 3.3 V ±2 %, 500 mA. CE is tied to the input, so U3 is always on when it has an input.

provenance.where: HX6211 datasheet (LCSC C296224): ±2 %, dropout 120 mV at 100 mA

checks.readsLowIf: U1 has no input (pin 4), or nothing connects PROG (pin 5) to GND: with PROG open the BL4054B shuts down

checks.expect: ≈0 V with no battery fitted (PROG follows the charge current: 1.0 V at the full current)

rails.notes: Charge current = 1000 × 1.0 V / R4 (2.2 kΩ) ≈ 455 mA. CHARGING1 (yellow) lights through R3 while U1 pulls pin 1 low. With no battery the simulator holds BAT at the float voltage; a real charger with nothing on BAT may cycle and flicker the LED.

provenance.where: Belling BL4054/BL4054B Rev 1.4: float 4.158–4.242 V, I = 1000 · V_PROG / R_PROG, PROG open = shutdown

notes: Power path, worked out from the board (derived): USB → D1 → +5V → D2 → U3 → +3.3V; +5V also → U1 → VBAT. Without USB, FET1 connects VBAT to U3's input.
No battery on the bench: the BAT pin shows the charger's float voltage. A charger that reads 0 V there with its input present has lost its PROG resistor, or is dead.

knowledge.title: OLIMEX ESP32-C3-DevKit-Lipo (Rev. D)

provenance.where: set points from github.com/OLIMEX/ESP32-C3-DevKit-Lipo @ 5d93e79 and the parts' datasheets (docs/calibration)

source.kind: bench supply, 5 V on the USB rail

rails.notes: VBUS of the USB-C connector USB-C1. R2 / R4 (5.1 kΩ) on CC1 / CC2 ask the host for 5 V.

checks.readsLowIf: nothing comes through D1 from USB

provenance.where: 1N5819 forward curve (Diodes DS30217); the drop depends on the load

source.kind: Schottky diode from +5V; FET1 from VBAT

checks.readsLowIf: D2 is open, +5V is low, or the buck draws far too much (a short on +3.3V)

checks.expect: 4.2–4.6 V (EN, tied to VIN on pin 4)

rails.notes: An unnamed net: U2's input. FET1 (IRLML6402, gate on +5V) feeds it from the battery when USB is absent.

provenance.where: D2, FET1 and U2 pins 1 / 4 share this net

checks.readsLowIf: something on the rail pulls it down (thermal camera: the hot part), or U2 has no input

rails.notes: Set point: 0.6 V × (1 + R10 220 kΩ / R11 49.9 kΩ) = 3.245 V. A rail that sits near the buck's input (≈4.5 V) means the divider is wrong: U2 then runs at full duty and passes its input through. Into a short U2 holds its 3.5 A current limit (SY8089A: hiccup mode on a real part).

provenance.where: SY8089 VREF 0.588–0.612 V (Silergy AN_SY8089/A Rev. 0.9A); R10 / R11 as designed

checks.readsLowIf: U1 has no input (pin 4), or PROG (pin 5) has no resistor to GND

checks.expect: ≈0 V with no battery fitted (PROG follows the charge current: 1.0 V at the full current)

rails.notes: Charge current = 1000 V / R5 (10 kΩ) = 100 mA. CHARGING1 lights through R3 while U1 pulls CHRG (pin 1) low. VBAT has no capacitor of its own on this board.

provenance.where: ShenZhen TPOWER TP4054 V2.2: float 4.158–4.242 V, R_PROG = 1000 V / I_BAT

notes: Power path, worked out from the board (derived): USB-C → D1 → +5V → D2 → U2 (buck) → +3.3V; +5V also → U1 → VBAT. Without USB, FET1 connects VBAT to U2's input.
A warm board with a low 3.3 V rail: find the hot part before replacing anything. After a repair, measure the rail again: two faults can hide behind each other.

knowledge.title: ESP32-C3-DevKit-RUST-1 (Rust ESP Board, rev. 1.2a)

provenance.where: set points from github.com/esp-rs/esp-rust-board @ efe1e8a and the parts' datasheets (docs/calibration)

source.kind: bench supply, 5 V at the USB-C connector

rails.notes: VBUS straight from J1. D7 (LESD5D5.0, 5 V TVS) protects it; D6 (B5819W) is the input diode.

checks.readsLowIf: D6 or one of its joints is open

rails.notes: Feeds the charger U6, the charge LED D3, Q1's gate and, through D4, +5V.

provenance.where: B5819W forward curve (MDD Rev 2025A4); the drop depends on the load

source.kind: Schottky diode from VBUS; Q1 from +BATT

checks.readsLowIf: D4 is open: the board then runs from the charger through Q1's body diode and +5V sits near 3.6–3.8 V

rails.notes: Two Schottky drops below the connector. Q1 (DMG3415U, gate on VBUS) connects the battery when USB is absent; its body diode conducts from +BATT to +5V even when it is off.

provenance.where: D4, Q1 (gate on VBUS) and U5 pin 4 share this net

checks.readsLowIf: U5 has no input (pin 4), its enable (pin 1, pulled up by R1 from +5V) is low, or the rail is shorted

rails.notes: Set point: 0.6 V × (1 + R2 100 kΩ / R3 22.1 kΩ) = 3.315 V. The ESP32-C3 module, the sensors (U1 SHTC3, U2 ICM-42670-P) and the RGB LED run from it.

provenance.where: SY8088 VREF 0.588–0.612 V (Silergy AN_SY8088 Rev. 0.1); R2 / R3 as designed

source.kind: 10 kΩ pull-up from +3V3, C10 (1 µF) delay

checks.readsLowIf: something leaks it to ground (residue around C10, a leaky C10, SW1 stuck): below 0.75 × 3.3 V the ESP32-C3 stays in reset and draws almost nothing

rails.notes: A running ESP32-C3 draws tens of mA (82 mA listening on Wi-Fi, datasheet); held in reset, the supply current drops to a few hundred µA while every rail looks fine.

provenance.where: ESP32-C3-MINI-1 datasheet v1.7 (EN pin 8, VIH 0.75 × VDD, RX 82 mA); R8 / C10 / SW1 on this net

checks.expect: ≈0 V with no battery fitted (PROG follows the charge current)

rails.notes: Charge current = 1000 V / R9 (10 kΩ) = 100 mA. With no battery fitted nothing defines +BATT (the charger is in constant-voltage mode, Q1 is off): a meter reads it somewhere between the 4.2 V float and +5V. Measure it with a battery or a load on it.

provenance.where: Microchip MCP73831/2 DS20001984G: VREG 4.168–4.232 V (-2), I_REG = 1000 V / R_PROG

notes: Power path, worked out from the board (derived): USB-C → D6 → VBUS → D4 → +5V → U5 (buck) → +3V3 → R8 → CHIP_PU; VBUS also → U6 → +BATT. Without USB, Q1 connects +BATT to +5V.
Rails present but no current: the chip is in reset. A low +5V with a healthy VBUS: the power is coming from the battery side.

knowledge.title: Rana Tadpole V2 (pocket controller, RP2040)

provenance.where: github.com/rana-sylvatica/rana-tadpole @ db1d5a5 (schematic LCSC codes) and the parts' datasheets (docs/calibration)

source.kind: bench supply, 5 V on USB-C VBUS

rails.notes: VBUS of the USB-C connector J4 (also on the console cable header J3). U5 / U6 (USBLC6-2P6) protect the USB data lines and sit on VBUS too.

source.kind: LDO, XC6206P332MR (fixed 3.3 V; LCSC C5446 in the schematic)

checks.readsLowIf: U1 has no input (pin 3), the logic rail behind D1 is shorted, or U1 is dead

rails.notes: XC6206: 1 VSS, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN; no enable pin. It feeds the logic rail through the Schottky D1.

source.kind: Schottky diode from the LDO (B5819W, LCSC C8598)

checks.readsLowIf: D1 is open, or the LDO output is low

rails.notes: One Schottky drop below 3.3 V. The RP2040's IO, the button pull-ups and the 74LVC1G00 debounce latches run from it. On the console cable it comes from J3 pin 6 instead.

provenance.where: B5819W forward curve (MDD Rev 2025A4); the drop depends on the load

source.kind: RP2040 on-chip regulator (VREG_VIN pin 44 → VREG_VOUT pin 45)

checks.readsLowIf: a capacitor on the rail (C4, C5, C6) is shorted: the regulator then sits at its 100 mA limit and the chips feeding it warm up, while the shorted part stays cool. Find it with current injection (power off) or freeze spray

rails.notes: The RP2040 makes its own 1.1 V core supply; VREG_VOUT (45) is wired to DVDD (23, 50) on the board. A running RP2040 draws tens of mA here.

provenance.where: RP2040 Datasheet (2021-06-07): VREG_VOUT 1.1 V, 100 mA max; DVDD 0.99–1.21 V

notes: Power path, worked out from the board (derived): USB-C → U1 (XC6206) → D1 → 3vDiode → RP2040 (IO, and its regulator → +1V1). D2 runs from 3vDiode back to VBUS for the console-cable case.

Buttons: each mouse switch (common on GND) has two contacts with 10 kΩ pull-ups (e.g. SW2: R40, R41) into a pair of 74LVC1G00 gates that debounce it. The NO line (pad 2) reads ≈0 V while the button is pressed and the logic rail when released; the NC line (pad 3) the other way round (Kailh CMI126603D08: 1 COM, 2 NO, 3 NC). A NO line that stays high when pressed: a cracked switch joint.

source.kind: Schottky diode from the LDO (B5819W, LCSC C8598)

checks.readsLowIf: D1 is open, or the LDO output is low

rails.notes: One Schottky drop below 3.3 V. The RP2040's IO and the flash U4 run from it; the buttons go straight to RP2040 pins and use its internal pull-ups (firmware-enabled, not simulated).

provenance.where: B5819W forward curve (MDD Rev 2025A4); the drop depends on the load

source.kind: RP2040 on-chip regulator (VREG_VIN pin 44 → VREG_VOUT pin 45)

checks.readsLowIf: the logic rail is low, or a capacitor on +1V1 is shorted

provenance.where: RP2040 Datasheet (2021-06-07): VREG_VOUT 1.1 V, 100 mA max

knowledge.title: Solder and Flux

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.expect: ≈5.00 V with every LED lit (≈26 mA in all)
checks.readsLowIf: the bench supply is off or current-limited, or something downstream draws far more
0 V: nothing reaches D1 through R1 (an open joint on either side of R1); ≈5 V with D1 dark: D1's own cathode joint is open
0 V: nothing reaches D2 through R2 (an open joint on either side of R2); ≈5 V with D2 dark: D2's own cathode joint is open
0 V: nothing reaches D3 through R3 (an open joint on either side of R3); ≈5 V with D3 dark: D3's own cathode joint is open

notes: Through-hole parts are soldered on the bottom side: a dull, grainy joint there can look fine from the top and still be open.

knowledge.title: Heat and Time

provenance.where: part values from the board; readings from DEADBOARD's simulator on the working board

checks.expect: ≈5.00 V with every LED lit (≈17 mA in all)
checks.readsLowIf: the bench supply is off or current-limited, or something downstream draws far more
0 V: nothing reaches D1 through R1 (an open joint on either side of R1); ≈5 V with D1 dark: D1's own cathode joint is open
0 V: nothing reaches D2 through R2 (an open joint on either side of R2); ≈5 V with D2 dark: D2's own cathode joint is open

notes: Through-hole parts are soldered on the bottom side: a dull, grainy joint there can look fine from the top and still be open.
Soldered with 63/37 tin-lead (melts at 183 °C, 361 °F), as in NEETS Module 14 (public-domain US Navy textbook).
GND is a copper pour over the whole bottom side: a joint in it loses heat into the pour and needs more heat to solder than one on a thin track.
